issue.title: Shared Cargo target can link a core dependency that disagrees with the clean checkout
issue.description:
Observed while landing sase-xq; this is unrelated build verification work discovered by the land family after all feature phases completed.

At clean sase-core 2fba6e44810370c27beab563597667e1d1d35351 (0.32.34), monitor mnrvd8t6f7vt failed tests::directive_contract_and_completion_bindings_return_plain_json_shapes. The shared-target PyO3 executable returned a dispatch directive absent from that checkout's DIRECTIVES registry and expected fixture. The installed wheel matched the source without dispatch. Cargo rebuilt gateway/PyO3 while reusing sase_core from the host-wide target. The failed-source/binary comparison is preserved in file:explicit:f35ab27b0d533f91e34dd047.

On exactly the same main revision 34fb561dd and clean core revision, setting CARGO_TARGET_DIR to a fresh workspace-local directory made that test pass (115 PyO3 tests passed, 2 intentionally ignored), the entire core just check pass, and main just check-full pass. Successful monitor zxvt9tvkhjqy (2026-09-07 05:47:05Z--06:19:09Z) and actual revision prints are preserved in file:explicit:a1a95625a24c66474d13f3bc. No product source, directive fixture, or gate assertion changed between the two runs.

Confirmed observation: the reused compiled dependency did not match the audited source, and a fresh isolated build recovered. Suspected mechanism: cross-checkout stale Cargo artifact reuse in /mnt/poseidon/cargo-target. The precise invalidation mechanism and original artifact producer are not yet proven; diagnose those before choosing a durable repair. Do not add dispatch to the older source fixture to accommodate a wrong binary. Verify build/test entry points prevent this mismatch, preserving useful safe caching where possible. Include a reproducible regression covering the discovered mechanism.

Triage: searched all task statuses for the exact fixture, Cargo/shared targets, stale build/binary and cache contamination; swept last-week bug tasks; reviewed all 26 current active epic scopes plus xe.12. No exact task or credible causal epic owner. xe.12 adds dispatch, but there is no evidence it caused cache reuse. Canceled sase-im concerns duplicate packaging compile cost, and ready sase-v6 concerns failed LSP copy/install status; neither is this core test dependency correctness defect. Size large because the cache-invalidation root cause remains unresolved and needs planning.

task_type_fields.impact: Rust verification can test the wrong dependency source and block otherwise valid landings.
task_type_fields.repro: Monitor mnrvd8t6f7vt at core 2fba6e4 returned dispatch absent from source; unchanged-source isolated-target monitor zxvt9tvkhjqy passed. See both attached evidence artifacts; precise stale-cache reproduction remains to be established.

payload.description: Both are sase-core verification defects tied to the shared /mnt/poseidon Cargo target: sase-xw is stale artifact reuse from it, and this failure only appears under the CARGO_TARGET_DIR redirection used to work around it
